program: Five Keys Independence High School accredited secondary-credential pathway
decisionUnit: An additional learner earning a high-school diploma or equivalency because of one ADA-equivalent year of Five Keys Independence High School

bottomLine.interpretation: Five Keys Independence High School reported $37,213,618 of FY2024 total expense and 2,232.74 annual ADA, or about $16,667 per ADA-equivalent year. If one year raises secondary-credential completion by 10 percentage points relative to the learner's counterfactual, the conditional cost is about $166,672 per additional credential. Five Keys has not measured that causal effect, so the 5%, 10%, and 20% cases are decision scenarios; zero or harm remains plausible.

inputs.label: Illustrative gift
inputs.basis: Donor scenario, not published current funding room

inputs.label: FY2024 Five Keys Independence High total expense
inputs.basis: Audited combining schedule: $30,984,984 education plus $6,228,634 management and general. This is schoolwide historical expense, not incremental philanthropic cost.
inputs.confidence: high for audited accounting; low for marginal use

inputs.label: FY2024 annual average daily attendance
inputs.basis: Audited Schedule of Average Daily Attendance. ADA is an attendance-based funding denominator, not unique enrollment, dosage, or completed student-years.

inputs.label: Historical gross expense per ADA-equivalent year
inputs.basis: $37,213,618 divided by 2,232.74 annual ADA. This covers the whole school across counties, custody and community settings, and multiple educational outcomes.
inputs.confidence: moderate for historical intensity; low for marginal cost

inputs.label: Reported GED completers
inputs.basis: The 2024-25 FKIH LCAP reports 56 people passed all GED portions in 2022-23. It does not publish the eligible or tested denominator and is not used as a causal effect.

inputs.label: MFI-modeled additional credential probability per ADA-equivalent year
inputs.basis: A transparent decision range, not a Five Keys estimate or confidence interval. The midpoint assumes one additional credential for ten fully funded ADA-equivalent years; the endpoints assume one for twenty or five. No credible Five Keys comparison currently identifies this effect.

formula.rangeMethod: Fixed FY2024 gross historical expense intensity with favorable, midpoint, and cautious positive credential-effect scenarios
formula.denominatorBoundary: An additional secondary credential is not a unique life substantially bettered, a QALY, continuous employment, higher earnings, avoided custody, or a verified marginal seat.

externalContext.boundary: RAND pooled many older U.S. correctional-education programs, populations, definitions, and follow-up periods. Those results support the intervention class but are not entered into the Five Keys credential model and must not be read as Five Keys' effect, cost, or avoided-custody estimate.

nullEffectBoundary: The conditional dollar range excludes zero and harm. Five Keys reports no comparable group for credential completion, and ADA is not a participant count. If learners would have obtained credentials through another school, if short jail stays prevent sufficient dosage, if a gift displaces public charter revenue, or if an added ADA-equivalent year does not increase completion, additional credentials approach zero and no finite positive impact price exists.

publicContext.period: FY2024 audit and active San Francisco contract snapshot as of 2026-08-20

fundingRoom.boundary: The $100,000 scenario is illustrative. Five Keys does not publish a current, gift-restricted credential expansion plan, the seats or teacher time a private gift would add, the public charter reimbursement those seats would generate, or how a gift would avoid replacing city, county, state, federal, or restricted funding.
fundingRoom.requiredNext: Obtain a dated FKIH credential-pathway budget and $100K, $1M, and $10M cases; unique applicant-to-credential flow by custody and community setting; tested GED denominator; dosage; credible comparison; 6- to 36-month outcomes; incremental instructional and navigation cost; and a public-funding displacement rule.

excludedBenefits: The reported 26% or 17% recidivism rates as a causal Five Keys effect
The 56 GED completions as if all were caused by Five Keys or generated in San Francisco
Credits earned, attendance, instructional contact, and graduation ceremonies as final beneficiary outcomes
RAND's 12.9-point pooled reincarceration difference as if it were measured for Five Keys
Employment, earnings, avoided incarceration costs, public safety, family stability, confidence, and community spillovers
QALYs, WELLBYs, and mortality benefits inside the native credential model; the separate 10-QALY bridge applies an explicit external health transfer
